summary: Silver buffed to a bright, cool white mirror, as on cutlery, jewellery, trays and trophies.
_comment: Polished silver: silver freshly buffed, with no tarnish, the metal of cutlery, jewellery, trays and trophies (most of it sterling, 92.5% silver, 7.5% copper, whose polished face looks the same). Named Silver, not SterlingSilver, in line with the library's metals (Gold, Copper, Brass: the plain matter name; maintainer, 2026-10-19). Opaque, param-only: a solid metal with no texture of its own at this scale; the finish is the roughness. Base colour from Physically Based 'Silver'. APPROXIMATE: OpenPBR's metal edge tint (specular_color, the F82 tint) and the complex IOR are not carried by the library (F-LC-6). Tarnish (the yellow-to-black sulphide film silver grows in air) is not carried: the library has no tarnish layer. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): hairline scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints, gated by the Edges mask (its B channel is the broad corner band meant for a deposit, its A the open faces meant for handling marks, so dust takes slot 2 and fingerprints slot 3). Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Silver_Polished_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.note: roughness_const is not taken (the entry is an ideal mirror); the polish is the judgement below.
